newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries rise solidly, await Tues FOMC mtg.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries rise solidly, await Tues FOMC mtg.

text.p: U.S. government securities posted solid gains in light trading Monday, and analysts said thin volume should continue Tuesday ahead of a widely expected Federal Reserve interest rate hike.
"For today, it's a wait-and-see attitude," said Joe Abate, an economist at Lehman Brothers.
Although longer maturities continued to outperform the short end, bill prices shook off their recent pummelling and held firm.
The bellwether 30-year bond was up 17/32 at 96-08/32 to yield 6.92 percent. Six-month bill rates were off 1/32 at 5.34 percent, and one-year bills were off 2/32 at 5.51 percent.
Dealers digested the Treasury's weekly auction of $23.0 billion of three- and six-month bills without a hitch.
The Treasury sold three-month bills at 5.26 percent, a hair below analysts' projection of 5.27 percent. Six-month issues moved at 5.33 percent, as projected.
"Everyone knew the levels you had to bid if you wanted to buy," said Richard Schwarz, a trader at Zions First National Bank Capital Markets. "It came as advertised."
Dealer appetite appeared strong, but it was unclear whether retail buyers stepped in, Schwarz said.
Prices rose in the middle of the curve later in the day, a move traders attributed to a big buyer of five-year notes.
Despite the gains during the session, the market was not abandoning its pricing-in of a 25-basis-point tightening at Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee Meeting, experts said.
Thin volume exaggerated the price gains as market players bought on dips, said Kevin Flanagan, vice president and an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
"There's definitely an air of caution going into tomorrow's meeting. This (buying) is not anything significant," he said.
The tightly wound consensus that a rate hike is imminent should limit volatility somewhat if indeed the FOMC tightens on Tuesday, analysts said.
Even so, many experts said prices will have to come off, particularly in the short end.
Rates of six-month and one-year bills could use an additional seven to 10 basis points in order to draw retail buyers assuming a Fed hike, some analysts said.
Other issues may eventually trade off regardless of the FOMC's decision, they said.
A rate hike would confirm the Fed's anti-inflation vigilance, but it would also awaken fears of further credit tightenings.
"If we trade up, I think it would be a selling opportunity, but I don't see a huge selloff either," said Terrence Piggott, trading department manager at Daiwa Securities America Inc.

Besides the monetary policy meeting, the market will eye a $17.25 billion two-year note auction. The auction will most likely be held before the FOMC announcement, but that should not dissuade bidding, analysts said.
"We've had to bid before," said Dean Witter's Flanagan. "This is not something that's going to be a huge issue."

At 1700 EST/ 2200 GMT, three-month Treasury bills were off 2/32 at 5.24 percent. The two-year note was up 2/32 at 99-10/32 to yield 6.26 percent. The five-year was up 8/32 at 98-22/32 to yield 6.56 percent, and the 10-year was up 11/32 at 96-24/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
